title: Tooling: prune signed-sparse coefficient enumeration with exact stream equivalence
head: fb82f10732f051541f9a9a734fd6e2b13fe49aa1
body:
Tooling improvement; no new κ. The historical signed-sparse coefficient checker scans all `4^h` coordinate words before rejecting excessive degree. This change rejects impossible prefixes while preserving the exact ordered term stream, parity filter, feature guard and expansion cap.

At h=8, seven alternating-order runs measured enumeration speedups of 574x / 52x / 3.08x for q=2 / 4 / 8. These are millisecond-scale microbenchmarks. The standard complete audit measured 0.982x: **no end-to-end speedup is claimed**. All mathematical certificate fields are identical; two regenerated certificates change only the affected source hash.

Validation: exhaustive equivalence for all 13 admissible (h,q) pairs through h=8, pinned original implementation and complete audit comparison, 14 relevant tests, two deliberate factor corruptions rejected, and the 10 signed-sparse tests also passing under `python3 -O`. Reproduce with:

```sh
python3 -B research/signed-sparse-pruning/reproduce.py
```

Base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`. Seed 92, verification engineering. No pinned coordination issue; scope and candidate selection are recorded locally. Checked current PR metadata for overlap. Existing performance PRs address other routines. `upstream/` and selected frontier are unchanged; full repository verification and selected cold replay were not run for this historical helper change.

Evidence, exact source pins, limits and predecessor credit: `research/signed-sparse-pruning/README.md` and `RESULT.json`. Credits the existing signed-sparse construction integrated by Douglas R. Colkitt. Contribution by anudeepadi with substantial OpenAI Codex AI assistance; Apache-2.0.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
